clue.text: After drink, extremely lazy and fat

indicators.note: the next pieces come after the drink, so they are written behind it

parts.note: port is a fortified wine

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters, taken here from lazy

explanation.surface: Someone who drinks and lazes about ends up overweight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives the first and last letters of 'lazy', L and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a stout, heavily built person is fat.

clue.text: She confuses people about a couple of points

indicators.note: the mixed-up letters are placed around the two points
to confuse is to muddle, so the letters of people are mixed up

parts.note: E and N are two compass points, east and north

explanation.surface: Someone muddles a crowd over a pair of details.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confuses' rearranges the six letters into PELOPE; 'about' wraps that round the compass points east and north. 'She' is a whole-word definition by pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name, so the clue's pronoun stands for a woman, as in Odysseus's faithful wife.

clue.text: Charles II's favourite place in England

definitions.meaning: John Wilmot, Earl of ..., the rakish poet who was a courtier and favourite of King Charles II

explanation.surface: The king's best-loved spot in the country.
explanation.definitionFit: The earl took his title from the Kent city, so one name covers both the royal favourite and the town.

clue.text: Survive, after all

definitions.meaning: coming at the end, behind every other

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to endure; as an adjective it means final, coming after every other one.

clue.text: Work on ice breaker in a new wet suit

indicators.note: a breaker in something breaks into it, so the work is set inside the reworked letters
a new version of the words gives their letters in a fresh order

parts.note: op is the usual abbreviation of opus, a work

explanation.surface: A swimmer trying out a new wetsuit for breaking through ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges ICE and WET together into TWIECE, and 'breaker in' sets OP between TW and IECE. Reading 'ice breaker' as one unit is the trap.
explanation.definitionFit: A suit of two matching garments, jacket and trousers or a bikini-style swimsuit.

clue.text: Knew cry came from a woodpecker

indicators.note: the answer emerges from the letters of the two words, reshuffled

explanation.surface: A recognisable call was heard from a woodpecker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'came from' signals that the letters of KNEW CRY are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the wryneck is a small Eurasian bird of the woodpecker family, named for twisting its neck.

clue.text: One Shakespearean character to us appears successful

parts.note: Prospero is the magician-duke in The Tempest
taken as written

explanation.surface: A character from Shakespeare looks to be doing well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' simply joins the character's name to US.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a thriving, well-off business is doing well.

clue.text: Have a meal during the flight?

definitions.text: Have a meal during the flight?

parts.words: Have a meal during the flight?
parts.note: eating while aloft in a plane would be eating high in the air; the phrase really means finish all one's food

explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to finish off all the food on the plate, read as dining up in the sky.

clue.text: Former forward, and a very good one too

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
pert means cheeky or forward

explanation.surface: A former striker who was also a fine player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forward' looks like a football position but means bold or cheeky.
explanation.definitionFit: A highly skilled specialist is a very good practitioner of a craft.

clue.text: Persian governor gained his seat on rising equality

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed on another sits above it

parts.note: sat, past tense of sit, is to have taken a seat

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: par means equality, as in on a par

explanation.surface: An official in ancient Persia won his place on the strength of equality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns PAR into RAP in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A satrap was the governor of a province in the ancient Persian empire.

clue.text: Shift scenery as required

indicators.note: shifting things moves them about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Stagehands move the set as the play demands.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: something required is needed or essential.

clue.text: Where a washer is always available

definitions.text: Where a washer is always available

parts.words: Where a washer is always available
parts.note: a plumbing washer sits inside a faucet, and the phrase for a faucet position means always ready to draw on

explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: something kept ready for use, like beer drawn from the barrel, and a tap literally contains a washer.

clue.text: General's remains

definitions.meaning: belonging to Robert E. Lee, the Confederate general
dregs or sediment left at the bottom of wine

explanation.definitionFit: The possessive of the general's surname also spells the word for sediment left in a bottle.

clue.text: Consultation document on environmental -matters?

definitions.meaning: a UK government paper setting out proposals for public discussion
green means environmental, so a paper on ecology could be described this way

explanation.definitionFit: A British government's discussion document before legislation, and green as ecological suggests a paper on ecology.

clue.text: He wants a successful strike

parts.note: a strike here is a find of gold or oil, not a walkout

explanation.definitionFit: Someone searching for mineral deposits hopes to strike gold.

clue.text: A supporter of mine

parts.note: reads as a personal fan, but means a beam holding up a coal mine's roof

explanation.definitionFit: A timber prop holding up the roof of a mine tunnel.

clue.text: We hear an officer is at the heart of things

indicators.note: signals a word that sounds like the one written

parts.note: a colonel is a senior army officer, pronounced like the answer

explanation.surface: Word is that an officer is at the centre of events.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: the core or essential part of a matter, like the seed in a nut.

clue.text: Worthy -of consideration?

definitions.meaning: able to be estimated or reckoned up

explanation.definitionFit: It means deserving esteem, and read literally it means capable of being assessed.

clue.text: A piece from the Financial Times about scrap dealers?

indicators.note: the paper's initials are wrapped around the dealers

parts.note: FT is the newspaper's initials
ragmen collect and sell rags and scrap

explanation.surface: An article from the FT concerning scrap merchants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but wraps the paper's initials round the dealers; ragmen are rag-and-bone men, door-to-door buyers of scrap in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a broken-off bit or shard.

clue.text: Where you must go if you get time

definitions.text: Where you must go if you get time

parts.words: Where you must go if you get time
parts.note: time here is a jail sentence, as in doing time

explanation.definitionFit: A jail, where a convict sentenced to time is sent.

clue.text: Where to see women in retreat

definitions.text: Where to see women in retreat

parts.words: Where to see women in retreat
parts.note: retreat suggests withdrawal from battle but means a religious seclusion

explanation.definitionFit: A convent, where religious sisters live withdrawn from the world.

clue.text: Chaos caused by novice in boat

indicators.note: the novice is put inside the boat

parts.note: a cutter is a small single-masted vessel
L is a learner, from the British learner-driver plate

explanation.surface: A beginner on board causes havoc.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: an untidy mess, a jumble of things.

clue.text: Imagine an order to join the army

definitions.meaning: to bring to mind, as in summon up a memory

definitions.text: an order to join the army

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to summon to mind; as a noun it is a summons to military service.

clue.text: A plush arrangement, though only makeshift

indicators.note: an arrangement of the letters puts them in a new order

explanation.surface: A luxurious setup that is really only temporary.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: an improvised, temporary contraption.

clue.text: This is too small to be right

definitions.text: This is too small to be right

parts.words: This is too small to be right
parts.note: right refers to a right angle of ninety degrees, not correctness

explanation.definitionFit: Geometry: an angle under ninety degrees, so smaller than a right angle.

clue.text: The kind of crust found only on the best pies?

definitions.text: The kind of crust found only on the best pies?

parts.words: The kind of crust found only on the best pies?
parts.note: the top layer of pastry, also the phrase for the aristocracy, the best people

explanation.definitionFit: The top pastry layer, and the phrase for high society.

clue.text: Sticks around, looking complacent

indicators.note: turned around, the word is read backwards

parts.note: gums are adhesives, things that stick

explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns GUMS into the answer; 'looking' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: self-satisfied, pleased with oneself.

clue.text: Big name appears nightly

definitions.meaning: a celestial body seen in the night sky

explanation.definitionFit: A celebrity, and a heavenly body visible after dark.

clue.text: Strike about work? Get away with you!

indicators.note: the strike goes around the work

parts.note: to strike is to hit
op is the usual abbreviation of opus, a work

explanation.surface: A threatened walkout over work, and someone told to clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' suggests industrial action but means HIT. The answer is British slang for go away.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: British slang telling someone to go away.

clue.text: Quite composed and skilled, to be fair

indicators.note: composed means put together, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: able means skilled or capable

explanation.surface: Calm and competent, so treating people justly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' reads as calm but rearranges QUITE as EQUIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: just and impartial.

clue.text: Shows the harbour lights

parts.note: a port is a harbour
rays are beams of light

explanation.surface: A display of a harbour's lights at night.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: depicts or represents.

clue.text: Stop doing wrong?

parts.note: stop means halt, and police halt wrongdoers by taking them into custody

explanation.definitionFit: To halt something, and police detention of a wrongdoer.
